problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Strong convexity implies convexity on the feasible ball.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The hidden objective is continuously differentiable on ℝᵈ. On the closed unit ball it is 1/2-strongly convex and 4-Lipschitz, and its gradient is 2-Lipschitz.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: One call compares any ordered pair (x,y) in the ball and returns one bit. Given the pair and the preceding transcript, the probability of true is (1+ρ(f(x)−f(y)))/2. Each call uses a fresh i.i.d. seed. The algorithm may choose both points adaptively.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The feasible set for query points and outputs is the closed Euclidean unit ball centered at zero in public dimension d≥1.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StronglyConvexDueling.lean: Point, Ball, spec.Query, spec.Output. LongTails/Setups/FlatTransferDueling.lean: Params.nonzero, model, spec.publicInput.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The hidden transfer ρ is odd, nondecreasing, continuously differentiable, and bounded by |ρ|≤1 globally. For public k=2j with integer j≥0 and |t|≤1, it satisfies ((2j+1)/8)|t|^(2j)≤ρ′(t)≤(2j+1)/4. Thus j>0 permits a zero slope at the origin, while j=0 requires ρ′(0)≥1/8. The algorithm knows these bounds and ε.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable ball-valued point X. For a minimizer u over the ball, the loss is f(X)−f(u), with target 0<ε≤1/64.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output gap must be integrable and satisfy E[f(X)−f(u)]≤ε under the joint law of the algorithm seed and oracle seeds.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The comparison oracle reveals a single bit through a hidden transfer whose local derivative bounds depend on the public exponent 2j. This controls how informative comparisons can be for nearly equal objective values.

descriptionHtml:
Strongly Convex Minimization with Flat Comparisons

We minimize a continuously differentiable function f:Rd→R over the closed Euclidean unit ball B in dimension d≥1. On B, f is strongly convex and Lipschitz with Lipschitz gradient. At each queried pair x,y∈B, the oracle uses a fresh independent sample to return a sign with mean ρ(f(x)−f(y)). The unknown transfer function ρ is odd and nondecreasing, with a polynomial lower bound on its slope near zero. For 0<ε≤1/64, the goal is a feasible output x¯∈B with E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where x⋆ minimizes f on B and the expectation includes algorithm and oracle randomness.

Writing ∥⋅∥ for the Euclidean norm, the optimization problem is minx∈Bf(x),B={x∈Rd:∥x∥≤1}. The algorithm receives d, ε, the objective constants specified below, and the transfer parameters r=1, k=2j, c=(2j+1)/8, and M=(2j+1)/4, where j is a nonnegative integer.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Objective regularity and curvature). The function f belongs to C1(Rd). For every x,y∈B, |f(x)−f(y)|≤4∥x−y∥,∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤2∥x−y∥,f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+14∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 2 (Transfer function). The function ρ:R→[−1,1] is continuously differentiable, odd, and nondecreasing. Its derivative satisfies c|t|k≤ρ′(t)≤M,|t|≤r, with |t|0=1 for every t.

Assumption 3 (Comparison oracle). Let Z1,Z2,… be independent random variables with common law ν on a measurable space Z, independent of the algorithm’s randomness. On call i at an ordered pair (x,y)∈B×B, the oracle returns g(x,y,Zi), where g:B×B×Z→{−1,1} is jointly measurable. For every x,y∈B, EZ∼ν[g(x,y,Z)]=ρ(f(x)−f(y)).

After the allotted comparisons, the algorithm must return a measurable B-valued output x¯. Its gap relative to a minimizer x⋆∈argminx∈Bf(x) must be integrable and satisfy E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Wataru Kumagai. Regret Analysis for Continuous Dueling Bandit. 2017. Complexity: Ω(d2/ε2) pairwise comparisons are necessary for expected objective gap at most ε, for 0<ε<0.004, under a fixed budget and a Gaussian comparison link with variance 2.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊d265536⋅(2⋅j+1)2⋅ε2⌋+

comparisonHtml:
On the closed Euclidean unit ball Bd, d≥1, the C1 loss is 1/2-strongly convex, 2-smooth and 4-Lipschitz. Each comparison uses fresh IID randomness and returns a sign with conditional mean ρ(f(x)−f(y)). The odd, nondecreasing C1 link satisfies |ρ|≤1 and q|t|2j/8≤ρ′(t)≤q/4 for |t|≤1, where q=2j+1 and j∈{0,1,…}. The target for any randomized adaptive algorithm is x^∈Bd with E[f(x^)−minBdf]≤ε, 0<ε≤1/64.

Necessary comparison budgets for flat-transfer dueling.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) LocalReferenceDuelingLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) Lower bound Ω(1+d2q2ε2) comparisons.
(2) (Kumagai 2017, Thm. 14) Lower bound Ω(d2/ε2) for ε<0.004 on Bd with variance-2 probit feedback. (1) proves fixed-ball hardness even for ρ(t)=14arctan⁡(tq), flat at ties for j≥1. At j=0 it matches the order of (2) under different normalizations. (1) uses 2-smooth losses. (2) allows 3.5-smooth losses and fixes ρ′(0)=1/π, outside the link envelope of (1).
(3) (Jamieson et al. 2012, Thm. 1, Lem. 1) Lower bound Ω(d/ε2q) for fixed q=κ−1 and margin parameters, d≥8 and sufficiently large T. (1) establishes hardness on a fixed ball in every dimension. The query cube in (3) shrinks with T, so the rates are not directly comparable. (1) fixes the local slope bounds and window. (3) allows any comparison oracle satisfying its reliability margin.

Abbr: T counts one-bit comparisons. κ−1 is the power of the absolute loss difference in the reliability margin.

Jamieson, Kevin G., Robert D. Nowak, and Benjamin Recht. 2012. “Query Complexity of Derivative-Free Optimization.” Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 25. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1209.2434.
Kumagai, Wataru. 2017. “Regret Analysis for Continuous Dueling Bandit.” Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1711.07693.
source:
import LongTails.Setups.StronglyConvexDueling

open OracleTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.FlatTransferDueling

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero d]
  j : ℕ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.nonzero

noncomputable def model (p : Params) : StronglyConvexDueling.Params where
  d := p.d
  μ := 1/2
  L := 2
  G := 4
  r := 1
  c := (2 * (p.j : ℝ) + 1) / 8
  M := (2 * (p.j : ℝ) + 1) / 4
  k := 2 * p.j
  ε := p.ε

noncomputable abbrev spec : Setup :=
  { StronglyConvexDueling.spec with
    Params := Params
    publicInput := model
    valid := fun p => 0 < p.ε ∧ p.ε ≤ 1/64
    admissible := fun p => StronglyConvexDueling.spec.admissible (model p)
    successful := fun p => StronglyConvexDueling.spec.successful (model p) }

end LongTails.Setups.FlatTransferDueling
